content: Initiating insulin therapy in adults with type 2 diabetes who have advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) requires careful consideration. Special caution should be exercised in individuals who are prone to hypoglycemia or have other relevant risk factors. The decision to initiate insulin must take into account the patient’s specific metabolic condition and overall health status. In cases where excessive basal insulin dosing, also known as overbasalization, is present, it is important to assess its impact. If significant hyperglycemia occurs during the night (nocturnal hyperglycemia) or before meals (preprandial hyperglycemia), the basal insulin dose should be carefully evaluated and potentially reduced to avoid overtreatment and associated complications.
